- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ 0.33) and price is falling, model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent sentiment swings; smooth forecasts by averaging last 3–5 periods if sentiment volatility > 0.5.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if price deviates > 3σ from 18-day moving average, apply mean-reversion bias correction.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2% to catch momentum.
